_comment: Per-platform capability matrix for oga-re. The purpose is that Hermes can ask THIS file how to unpack a game, which CPU architecture to use, which Ghidra loader applies, which emulator can supply runtime memory, and whether a matching decompilation already exists — instead of holding that knowledge per game. Expand only with CONFIRMED information; `status` values are honest, and 'research_needed' is a real answer, not a placeholder to be quietly upgraded.

statusLegend.ready: tooling identified AND verified working on this machine
statusLegend.partially_ready: some tooling verified; a documented gap remains
statusLegend.research_needed: not yet established; do not claim support
statusLegend.blocked_version_conflict: tooling exists but requires a Ghidra version incompatible with something else in the workflow

nds.name: Nintendo DS
loaders: dsd-ghidra v0.7.0 (dsd-aware: syncs functions, data symbols, sections, delinks, relocations and overlay/autoload mapping from a ds-decomp project)
NTRGhidra v1.5.1 (standalone DS ROM loader; adds dynamic overlay load/unload and a bundled ARM9/ARM7 hardware-register label set + Function ID database)

runtimeAccess.melonDS: in-process memory access via its MainRAM pointer (used today by the OGA harnesses); also has a debugger. No gdbstub needed for our reads.

nds.symbolInterchange: dsd-ghidra consumes the decomp project's own config.yaml + symbols.txt directly — the strongest symbol-interchange path of any platform here

matchingDecomp.licence: NONE — no LICENSE/COPYING file, no SPDX headers, GitHub API license: null. All rights reserved by the author. CITE addresses and symbol names as research reference; do NOT copy code, headers or config files into this project.
matchingDecomp.modules: arm9 main + ITCM + DTCM autoloads + 12 ARM9 overlays (ov000-ov011). ARM7 is NOT represented at all.
matchingDecomp.buildRequires: Python 3.11+, GCC 9+, Ninja, and the MetroWerks mwccarm 2.0/sp2p2 compiler (auto-downloaded; run through Wibo or Wine on non-Windows). Not a Makefile project — `python tools/configure.py YFEE01 && ninja`.
matchingDecomp.completeness: ~15-20% roughly, and not an official match percentage: 20,982 symbol lines across 15 symbols.txt, 12,328 functions of which 10,559 are still auto-named func_* and 1,769 carry real names. Hand-written decompiled code in ~49 src/ files (about 1,939 definitions). Deep on arm9 core + ov000; zero hand-written src for ov001-ov004, ov006, ov007, ov009-ov011.

blockers: ddsd-ghidra requires Ghidra 11.2.1, which scoop does not carry — it must be downloaded manually from GitHub releases.
dsd-ghidra's symbol sync is GUI-only (Swing file chooser, no headless path). Automating it needs a custom wrapper around the dsdghidra.sync.* classes.
NTRGhidra requires Ghidra 12.0.4, so it cannot coexist with dsd-ghidra in one Ghidra install.

gb.name: Game Boy
gb.addressModelNote: Banked. A 16-bit address does NOT identify code without its bank — the same address exists in every bank. Must use bank:address, never a bare address.

gbc.name: Game Boy Color
gbc.addressModelNote: Banked, plus ROM and RAM banking. Same bank:address requirement as GB.

gba.name: Game Boy Advance
gba.ghidraNative: yes — Ghidra handles ARM and Thumb well, so this is a strong automation target

nes.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
nes.addressModelNote: Banked via mapper switching. Same bank-awareness problem as GB/SNES.

snes.name: Super Nintendo
snes.addressModelNote: Banked with LoROM / HiROM / ExHiROM mappings plus optional enhancement chips. A logical address is meaningless without its mapping and bank context.

genesis.name: Sega Genesis / Mega Drive
genesis.ghidraNative: yes — Ghidra ships 68000 support, so the main-CPU side is friendly

n64.name: Nintendo 64
n64.addressModelNote: ROM byte order varies (big-endian .z64 / byte-swapped .n64 / little-endian .v64) and code is loaded from overlays. Where Splat already provides segmentation and symbols, integrate rather than rediscovering.

ps1.name: PlayStation 1
ps1.ghidraNative: yes — Ghidra has MIPS support; the gap is executable-format handling
ps1.addressModelNote: PS-X EXE carries an explicit load address; overlays are loaded dynamically, so a file offset is not an address.

ps2.name: PlayStation 2
ps2.ghidraNative: partially — base MIPS yes, MMI and VU0 macro instructions need an extension

runtimeAccess.PCSX2: debugger, symbols, save states. Save-state-to-Ghidra correlation is the high-value path and is the reason PS2 matters for OGA (Budokai / Tenkaichi targets).

psp.name: PlayStation Portable
psp.ghidraNative: partially — base MIPS yes, Allegrex specifics and VFPU need an extension

runtimeAccess.PPSSPP: networked debugger/API, .sym symbol files, breakpoints/watchpoints, save states — the richest runtime bridge of the non-DS platforms, which makes PSP strategically important for OGA (Shin Budokai Another Road).

deferred._comment: Evaluated later. Listed so the intent is recorded without implying tooling exists. Deliberately deprioritised so future platform exploration does not distract from getting FE11 working first.
